decisions.why: Glossary (working): in ætérnum → eternamente, kept apart from in sǽculum → para sempre (118:44) on purpose. The stanza Lamed opens on it and says it twice more (118:89, 93, 98); Nun closes on it twice (118:111, 112). One slot, so that it can be switched through the portion.

options.label: eternamente
options.note: Draft 7, the glossary. In 118:93 "Eternamente não esquecerei" stands for the Latin's "In ætérnum non oblivíscar" (= never): the adverb first, as in 118:89, so that the stanza's anaphora is heard and so that it is not read as "I shall not forget for ever".

options.label: para sempre
options.note: Matos Soares, the Diurnal. Plainer and shorter; merges with in sǽculum.

decisions.latin: In generatiónem et generatiónem véritas tua
decisions.why: Two things: the idiom (in generatiónem et generatiónem) and the verbless colon. véritas → verdade (glossary; not the Hebrew-family "fidelidade").

options.label: De geração em geração é a vossa verdade

forms.v90a: De geração em geração é a vossa verdade

options.note: Draft 8. The stylist heard the verbless colon as "a sentence left to be completed". The copula is what D2 allows to be supplied, and the build is the one D14 ruled for the refrain (porque é para sempre a sua misericórdia): copula, span of time, subject last.

options.label: De geração em geração a vossa verdade

forms.v90a: De geração em geração a vossa verdade

options.note: Draft 7. "De geração em geração" is what Portuguese says for the phrase (Matos Soares, the Diurnal); the noun is still said twice, as in the Latin. No verb, as the Latin has none and Douay-Rheims keeps none ("Thy truth unto all generations").

options.label: Para geração e geração a vossa verdade

forms.v90a: Para geração e geração a vossa verdade

options.note: The Latin's build word for word. A calque.

options.label: A vossa verdade permanece de geração em geração

forms.v90a: A vossa verdade permanece de geração em geração

options.note: The stylist's line. Refused: it supplies pérmanet where the Latin has no verb, so that "permanece" would sound three times in 118:89–90 where the Latin has it twice.

decisions.why: ordinátio (διάταξις): an ordering, an arrangement, also an ordinance. The word study kept "ordem" free for this verse. "Ordenação" is heard today as the ordination of a priest.

options.label: Pela vossa ordem
options.note: Draft 7, Matos Soares ("Por tua ordem"). "Ordem" is both a command and an arrangement, which is the width of ordinátio.

options.label: Pela vossa ordenação
options.note: The cognate (Douay-Rheims "ordinance"); heard as holy orders.

options.label: Pela vossa disposição
options.note: The Greek's sense exactly; abstract.

decisions.why: The Greek has one verb three verses running (διαμένει, 118:89, 90, 91); the Latin says pérmanet, pérmanet, persevérat. The variation is the Latin's and costs nothing to keep.

options.label: persevera
options.note: Draft 7: the cognate, apart from "permanece" in 118:89–90. A day that "perseveres" is as unusual in Portuguese as in Latin.

options.label: continua
options.note: Matos Soares ("continua (o curso) dos dias"), Douay-Rheims "goeth on".

options.label: permanece
options.note: What the Greek says: the same verb a third time.

decisions.latin: Nisi quod lex tua meditátio mea est
decisions.why: The colon holds the formula lex tua meditátio mea est (118:77, 97, 174 → "a vossa lei é a minha meditação") inside nisi quod, with its indicative: "were it not that …". Draft 8: the slot now holds the whole verse, because the choice of the first colon decides whether the second may keep the Latin's order (meditação … humilhação rhyme at mediant and final).

options.label: Se a minha meditação não fosse a vossa lei

forms.nisi_quod: Se a minha meditação não fosse a vossa lei: * então talvez eu tivesse perecido {humilitate}

options.note: Draft 8. The stylist named draft 7 the worst line of the portion: "Não fosse que … é" asks for a mental correction in mid-speech, and the second colon was slowed by the insertion that had been put there to avoid a rhyme. His own line ("Se a vossa lei não fosse a minha meditação: … na minha humilhação") brings the rhyme back. This keeps his build and his second colon — which is the Latin's order — and turns the copular clause round instead: "my meditation" and "your law" are the same two terms of lex tua meditátio mea est, and either may be its subject. Cost: the formula of 118:77, 97, 174 is not word for word here; it could not be anyway, once the verb is a subjunctive.

options.label: Se a vossa lei não fosse a minha meditação

forms.nisi_quod: Se a vossa lei não fosse a minha meditação: * então talvez eu tivesse perecido {humilitate}

options.note: The stylist's line as he gave it; Matos Soares' build. Rhymes at mediant and final (meditação / humilhação), which the Latin does not.

options.label: Não fosse que a vossa lei é a minha meditação

forms.nisi_quod: Não fosse que a vossa lei é a minha meditação: * então, {humilitate}, talvez eu tivesse perecido

options.note: Draft 7: nisi quod word for word, with the formula whole. Refused by the stylist as unsayable.

decisions.latin: Me exspectavérunt peccatóres · ab exspectatióne mea
decisions.why: exspectáre / exspectátio meet twice in the portion. "Esperar / esperança" are taken: speráre → esperar em (118:42), spes → esperança (118:49), supersperáre → pôr toda a esperança em. The Greek keeps them apart as well (ὑπομένω, προσδοκία against ἐλπίζω).

options.label: aguardar · no que aguardo
options.note: Draft 8. The stylist found "na minha expectativa" bureaucratic and ill-joined to "envergonheis", and offered "pelo que espero". His clause is taken (it is Matos Soares' "no que espero", and the same turn D16 gives elóquium), but with exspectáre's own verb, so that 118:95 and 118:116 still share a root and speráre keeps "esperar".

options.label: aguardar · expectativa
options.note: Draft 7: the cognate noun. Understood by the blind reader ("do not let my hope be frustrated / do not let me be shamed for having hoped"); refused by the stylist as bureaucratic.

options.label: esperar · pelo que espero
options.note: The stylist's wording in both verses (Matos Soares: "esperaram-me", "no que espero"). Refused: it folds exspectáre into speráre, two verses after supersperávi (118:114), where Latin and Greek keep two verbs.

decisions.why: pérdere, to destroy; the Greek verb (ἀπολέσαι) is the active of the one behind periíssem three verses earlier (118:92 ἀπωλόμην → "perecido").

options.label: para me destruir
options.note: Draft 8, from the stylist, who found "para me fazer perecer" ceremonious and heavy (it was also +4 syllables). Douay-Rheims "to destroy me". The link with periíssem (118:92) is given up for the plainer of two faithful words (D2).

options.label: para me fazer perecer
options.note: Draft 7: kept pérdere beside períre → perecer, as Latin and Greek do. Heavy in the mouth (stylist).

options.label: para me perder
options.note: The cognate (Matos Soares). Heard today as "to lose me", or "to lead me astray".

decisions.why: consummátio: Lewis & Short "a finishing, completing, accomplishing, consummation" (συντέλεια). Everything that is brought to completion has an end; the commandment has none. In Brazil "consumação" is first of all what one eats and drinks in a bar (consumação mínima), being also the noun of "consumir".

options.label: Vi o fim de toda perfeição

forms.consummationis: Vi o fim de toda perfeição

options.note: Draft 7, Matos Soares ("o fim de tudo o que é perfeito"). "Perfeição" is per-féctio, a thing carried through to its finish — the same picture as con-summátio, in a word that is heard rightly. (The Diurnal has the same words from the Hebrew; that proves nothing about sense.) Draft 8: natural order, from the stylist.

options.label: Vi o fim de toda consumação

forms.consummationis: Vi o fim de toda consumação

options.note: The cognate; church Portuguese knows "a consumação dos séculos". Risk: heard as consumption.

options.label: Vi o fim de todo acabamento

forms.consummationis: Vi o fim de todo acabamento

options.note: Would answer 118:87 "acabaram comigo" and keep the Latin's echo; but "acabamento" is a builder's finish.

options.label: De toda perfeição vi o fim

forms.consummationis: De toda perfeição vi o fim

options.note: Draft 7: the Latin's order. The stylist: the inversion piles up literary solemnity. Order is the ear's (D2).

decisions.why: Two words. latum: the glossary has latitúdo → amplidão (117:5, 118:45), so the adjective is "amplo". nimis (σφόδρα, "exceedingly"): the glossary says it has no one rendering — 118:4 custodíri nimis is "à risca", which cannot serve here; that is why this is a decision of its own and not a slot of "nimis".

options.label: é muito amplo
options.note: Draft 8, the stylist's: "sobremaneira calls more attention to itself than the image of breadth does"; the blind reader listed it as a word an ordinary hearer might not know; and the colon was +6. nimis is "very, exceedingly" (σφόδρα), no more.

options.label: é amplo sobremaneira
options.note: Draft 7: the glossary's literal for nimis. Refused by the stylist, unknown to the blind reader, +6 syllables.

options.label: é largo sobremaneira
options.note: "Largo" is the first word for latus; it breaks the family with "amplidão".

options.label: não tem limites
options.note: Matos Soares ("somente a tua lei não tem limites"). Refused: it explains the image instead of giving it.

decisions.why: The Latin prints a question mark, but it is an exclamation (Greek ὡς ἠγάπησα; Douay-Rheims "O how have I loved thy law, O Lord!"). With "?" the Portuguese would be read as a real question — "in what way did I love?" — so the verse ends in "!".

options.label: Como amei
options.note: Draft 7: quómodo is "como", and "Como amei …!" is a natural exclamation. The perfect is kept (diléxi), as in 118:47–48 "que eu amei".

options.label: Quanto amei
options.note: The Diurnal's word; the commoner exclamation of degree.

decisions.latin: Super inimícos meos · Super omnes docéntes me · Super senes
decisions.why: Three verses of Mem open on Super (ὑπέρ, "more than"); the anaphora is kept identical. 118:72 already has super míllia → "mais que milhares", and 118:103, 127 follow. Draft 8: the stylist asked for natural order in all three verses (the comparison comes before one knows what is compared; the verb arrives late). The previous portion met the same question in Daleth (five verses opening on Viam) and ruled for natural order with the Latin's order as the option; the same is done here. "Mais que" is still said in each of the three verses.

options.label: natural order

forms.sup98: {m_Sg_por} me fizestes mais prudente que os meus inimigos
forms.sup99: Entendi mais que todos os que me ensinam

options.note: Draft 8, the stylist's three lines. Order is the ear's (D2); it also removes the second reading the blind reader found in 118:98 ("you did more for my prudence than my enemies did").

options.label: "Mais que" first, as in the Latin

forms.sup98: Mais que os meus inimigos me fizestes prudente {m_sg_por}
forms.sup99: Mais que todos os que me ensinam entendi

options.note: Draft 7: the anaphora Super … Super … Super at the head of three verses.

options.label: "Acima de" first

forms.sup98: Acima dos meus inimigos me fizestes prudente {m_sg_por}
forms.sup99: Acima de todos os que me ensinam entendi

options.note: The preposition kept as a preposition (Douay-Rheims "above ancients"). With "me fizestes prudente" it reads as rank rather than degree.

decisions.why: senes, old men (πρεσβυτέρους).

options.label: anciãos
options.note: Draft 7, Matos Soares. The respectful word, and the one that carries "those whose age should make them wise". It will be shared with senióres (104:22, 106:32).

options.label: velhos
options.note: The plain word; in Brazil it sounds dismissive, which the verse is not.

decisions.why: A dative of possession: the commandment "is to me" for ever — mine, or with me. The subject is the singular mandátum.

options.label: ele é meu
options.note: The dative of possession as Portuguese says it (the Diurnal: "é para sempre meu"). "Ele" names the subject, which can only be "o vosso mandamento". Draft 8: the adverb last, from the stylist.

options.label: ele está comigo
options.note: Douay-Rheims "it is ever with me".

options.label: eternamente ele é meu
options.note: Draft 7: the Latin's order (in ætérnum first).

decisions.latin: Ab omni via mala prohíbui pedes meos
decisions.why: prohibére, to hold back (ἐκώλυσα). "Afastar" is taken twice over (amovére, repéllere), "desviar" is avértere's, "deter-se" is stare's in Ps 1:1.

options.label: retive
options.note: Draft 7: Douay-Rheims "restrained". To hold the feet back from a road.

options.label: afastei
options.note: Natural (Matos Soares "Retirei"), but it is the verb of 118:29 Viam iniquitátis ámove a me, and a third Latin verb on it.

decisions.latin: Quam dúlcia fáucibus meis elóquia tua
decisions.why: The exclamation, verbless in Latin. D2: of two faithful wordings the plainer.

options.label: Como os vossos ditos são doces
options.note: Draft 8: the stylist's order (subject before "à minha garganta", so that the verse is understood as it goes). His noun, "as vossas palavras", is refused — it is D16's ruling that the plural elóquia stays "os vossos ditos", and "palavras" remains one touch away in decision "eloquia".

options.label: Como são doces … os vossos ditos
options.note: Draft 7: the Latin's order, subject last.

options.label: Quão doces são … os vossos ditos
options.note: Matos Soares, the Diurnal. "Quão" is understood and liturgical, but nobody says it.

decisions.why: fauces: Lewis & Short "the upper part of the throat … the pharynx, throat, gullet"; the Greek λάρυγξ. The verse names two organs, throat and mouth. Rule 5: concrete images stay concrete.

options.label: à minha garganta
options.note: Draft 7: the Latin's (and the Greek's) organ. Sweetness going down the throat is the stranger picture and the Latin's own.

options.label: ao meu paladar
options.note: Douay-Rheims "palate", Matos Soares, the Diurnal — every version. Where taste is felt; the natural word.

decisions.why: lucérna, an oil lamp. The copula is supplied ("é"), as Matos Soares does. lumen → luz (glossary).

options.label: Lâmpada
options.note: Draft 7: Matos Soares and the Diurnal alike; the word by which the verse is known. Proparoxytone, but at the head of the verse, not at a cadence.

options.label: Candeia
options.note: Exactly an oil lamp, and paroxytone; rustic and fading from use.

decisions.why: statúere with an infinitive is Lewis & Short's second sense, "to decide, determine, resolve". In 118:38 (Státue servo tuo elóquium tuum → Firmai) it is the first sense, to establish. The Greek has one verb in both (ἔστησα / στῆσον); Portuguese has none that does both.

options.label: e resolvi
options.note: Draft 8. The stylist heard "determinei" as administrative, and both he and the blind reader noted that it can be heard as an order given to someone. He offered "decidi": the sense is taken, in the verb that is not also a vós imperative ("decidi" = "decide ye"; "resolvi" is not, the imperative being "resolvei"). Lewis & Short: "to decide, determine, resolve".

options.label: e determinei
options.note: Draft 7, Matos Soares. Can be heard as "I gave the order that".

options.label: e firmei
options.note: The glossary row (statúere → firmar, which foresaw this verse): keeps the echo of 118:38. But "firmei guardar" is not Portuguese; it would need a supplied noun ("firmei o propósito de").

options.label: e decidi
options.note: The stylist's word. Equal in sense to "resolvi"; passed over only because "decidi" is also the vós imperative of decidir.

decisions.why: A neuter plural adjective used as a noun: "the voluntary things of my mouth" — τὰ ἑκούσια, the free-will offerings of the Law, here offered by the mouth. Douay-Rheims "The free offerings of my mouth"; Matos Soares "a oferta espontânea da minha boca".

options.label: as ofertas voluntárias
options.note: Draft 7: the noun supplied, as both Vulgate-family versions supply it (compare 117:27b, where "ramos" is supplied with Douay-Rheims); the Latin's adjective kept.

options.label: as coisas voluntárias
options.note: Nothing supplied but "coisas" (the neuter plural said literally). Hard to follow.

options.label: as ofertas de livre vontade
options.note: With the glossary's voluntárie → de livre vontade (53:8). Four syllables longer in an already long colon.

decisions.why: beneplácita fácere, to make well-pleasing (εὐδόκησον, be pleased with). "Agradável" is jucúndus's (118:39).

options.label: Fazei que vos agradem
options.note: Draft 8. The stylist refused "Fazei bem aceitas" as an unspontaneous combination and offered "Aceitai com agrado", which drops fac. This keeps fac as "fazei" and says plácita with the verb Portuguese has for placére (agradar); it is Matos Soares' build ("Faze, Senhor, que te seja agradável") without spending jucúndus's adjective. "Bene" is carried by the verb itself.

options.label: Fazei bem aceitas
options.note: Draft 7: bene-plácita part by part. Refused by the stylist ("pouco espontânea").

options.label: Tornai agradáveis
options.note: Douay-Rheims "make acceptable", Matos Soares "que te seja agradável". Spends jucúndus's word.

options.label: Aceitai com agrado
options.note: The stylist's line; what the Greek says (the Diurnal: "aceita"). Drops fac; kept as an option.

decisions.why: láqueus → laço (glossary, Ps 90:3). The verb: pónere.

options.label: puseram um laço para mim
options.note: Draft 7: pónere → pôr, the plain verb, with the dative as "para mim".

options.label: me armaram um laço
options.note: The idiom (Matos Soares "armaram-me laços", Douay-Rheims "laid a snare").

decisions.why: erráre de, to stray from (πλανάομαι). The verb returns in the last verse of the psalm (118:176 Errávi sicut ovis quæ périit), so the word chosen here should serve there. "Desviar" is avértere's, "apartar-se" declináre's, "afastar" amovére's.

options.label: não me extraviei
options.note: Draft 7: to go off the road, of sheep and of men; fits 118:176 (Extraviei-me como ovelha).

options.label: não errei
options.note: The cognate; "errar" is first "to make a mistake", so it needs "para longe" to be heard as wandering.

options.label: não me desviei
options.note: The natural word (Matos Soares "não me afastei"); it is avértere's in this psalter.

decisions.why: fácere with the law-word as object. "Fazer os preceitos" is not Portuguese; the light verb yields, as in 118:65 (bonitátem fácere → usar de bondade). "Praticar" is operári's (praticar a iniquidade). "Cumprir" is safe here, being an infinitive (the vós imperative "cumpri" is a rule-3 trap, as the previous portion noted).

options.label: para cumprir
options.note: Draft 7: what one does with a precept in Portuguese. "Para" repeats the build of 118:36 (Inclinai o meu coração para …).

options.label: a praticar
options.note: Matos Soares. Operári's verb.

options.label: para fazer
options.note: The Latin's verb (Douay-Rheims "to do thy justifications"). A calque.

decisions.latin: Iníquos ódio hábui · omnem viam iníquam ódio hábui (118:104 has odívi)
decisions.why: The Latin has odívi in 118:104 and ódio hábui in 118:113, 128 (and 118:163 to come); the Greek has ἐμίσησα every time. Odísse has no perfect of its own, and ódio habére supplies one: the variation is the Latin translator's, with no difference of sense — D15's test for sermo, applied to a verb. Draft 8: the stylist faulted both verses for a proparoxytone at the cadence (iníquos at the mediant of 118:113, iníquo at the end of 118:128). For 118:113 he offered "Aos iníquos tive ódio" — which is the Latin word for word (Iníquos ódio hábui), periphrasis and order. The same is done in 118:128, so the draft returns to keeping ódio habére apart from odívi (118:104 "odiei"), now for the ear's sake as well as the Latin's.

options.label: tive ódio (the Latin's order)

forms.odio128: a todo caminho iníquo tive ódio

options.note: Draft 8, from the stylist (118:113): both cadences now fall on "ódio", a paroxytone, as the Latin's fall on ódio hábui.

options.label: odiei
options.note: Draft 7: one verb, as the Greek and every version. Leaves a proparoxytone at the mediant of 118:113 and at the end of 118:128.

options.label: odiei todo caminho de iniquidade (118:128)
options.note: The stylist's cure for 118:128. Refused: it makes 118:128b word for word 118:104b, where the Latin differs (viam iníquam / viam iniquitátis).

decisions.latin: Súscipe me secúndum elóquium tuum, et vivam · Súscipe servum tuum in bonum
decisions.why: suscípere → amparar is settled (D19), with suscéptor → amparo — which stands two verses earlier (118:114 suscéptor meus), so noun and verb answer each other here as in Ps 3. Made a decision because 118:116 is a verse with a life of its own: from general knowledge (not verified on disk), it is the Suscipe sung at monastic profession, where it is understood as "receive me".

options.label: Amparai
options.note: Draft 7, D19; Matos Soares has "Ampara-me" and "Ampara o teu servo". Safe at the vós imperative. The Greek (ἀντιλαβοῦ, take hold of to help) is this sense.

options.label: Recebei
options.note: The other sense of suscípere, and how the verse is heard at a profession. It would break the pair with 118:114 "o meu amparo".

options.label: Sustentai
options.note: Douay-Rheims "Uphold"; the Diurnal "Sustenta-me".

decisions.why: discédere a, to go away from (ἀποστατέω). The psalm's other verbs of leaving are declináre a → apartar-se de, derelínquere → abandonar, erráre de → extraviar-se de.

options.label: os que se afastam
options.note: Draft 7: the natural verb. It is the reflexive of "afastar", which already serves amovére and repéllere (transitive, of God acting); here men remove themselves.

options.label: os que se retiram
options.note: A verb of its own (6:9 Discédite a me will want "Retirai-vos de mim"); "retirar-se dos juízos" is odd.

options.label: os que se desviam
options.note: Matos Soares. Avértere's verb.

decisions.why: The Latin's reading (with the Greek: παραβαίνοντας ἐλογισάμην), not the Hebrew's dross. prævaricári, to walk crookedly, to transgress; reputáre, to reckon. In Brazil "prevaricação" is a civil servant's crime of neglecting his duty. "Considerar" is consideráre's.

options.label: Tive por transgressores
options.note: Draft 7. "Transgressores" is the Greek's word and the plain one (D2: of two faithful words the plainer); "ter por" is reputáre without a learned verb.

options.label: Tive por prevaricadores
options.note: The cognate (Douay-Rheims "prevaricators", Matos Soares). Heard as a term of administrative law.

options.label: Reputei como prevaricadores
options.note: Matos Soares word for word.

decisions.why: The Latin's reading (the Hebrew has the flesh bristling with dread). confígere: Lewis & Short "to fasten together; to pierce through, transfix"; the Greek καθήλωσον is "nail down". Both verbs are safe at the vós imperative.

options.label: Traspassai
options.note: Draft 7: Douay-Rheims "Pierce", Matos Soares "Traspassa". With "com o vosso temor" as the weapon.

options.label: Cravai
options.note: The Greek's nails, which the Fathers heard here; but "cravar" wants the thing driven in as its object (cravar o temor nas carnes), which would turn the Latin's syntax round.

options.label: Atravessai
options.note: The blind reader listed "Traspassai" among words an ordinary hearer might not know. "Atravessar" is the everyday verb for running something through. Not taken: "traspassar" is the word Portuguese keeps for exactly this (a sword through a soul), and the reader's paraphrase shows he understood it.

decisions.why: timére a + ablative: the glossary (Ps 90, open) turns it into a direct object. enim → pois.

options.label: pois temi os vossos juízos
options.note: Draft 7, the glossary; Matos Soares "porque temi os teus juízos".

options.label: pois dos vossos juízos tive temor
options.note: Keeps the preposition and the Latin's order, and echoes "temor" in the first colon as tímui echoes timóre.

decisions.why: The biblical pair judícium et justítia with fácere. The same verb and noun as 118:84 (quando fácies … judícium?): he has done judgment and asks when God will.

options.label: Fiz juízo e justiça
options.note: Draft 7: fácere → fazer, so that it answers 118:84 "fareis juízo"; without articles, as the pair is said.

options.label: Pratiquei o juízo e a justiça
options.note: Matos Soares' verb ("Tenho praticado a rectidão e a justiça"). Operári's verb in this psalter; loses the answer to 118:84.

decisions.latin: calumniántibus me · non calumniéntur me supérbi
decisions.why: calumniári: Lewis & Short "to accuse falsely … to practise chicanery … to misrepresent". The Greek behind it has two verbs (ἀδικοῦσιν, συκοφαντησάτωσαν) and the Hebrew means to oppress; the Latin says slander, twice.

options.label: caluniar
options.note: Draft 7: the Latin's word, twice, as the Latin has it; Matos Soares, Douay-Rheims ("slander … calumniate").

options.label: oprimir
options.note: The Hebrew's sense (the Diurnal: "opressores … não me oprimam"). Refused: not what the Latin says.

decisions.why: D16 names this verse: the singular elóquium with a genitive, where the clause "o que dissestes" cannot simply stand. The genitive is open — the utterance that belongs to your justice, that your justice spoke, or that is just (Douay-Rheims "the word of thy justice"; Matos Soares "das promessas da tua justiça").

options.label: pelo dito da vossa justiça
options.note: Draft 7: the noun, as D16 allows ("dito available"). It keeps the genitive as open as the Latin has it, and the root of "os vossos ditos" / "o que dissestes". This form follows decision "eloquia" (and, for its preposition, "deficere_in"). Draft 8: the stylist refused it ("sounds like a reference to a quoted phrase") and asked for "pela palavra da vossa justiça" — D16's named retreat, which is not mine to take in one verse; it is the fourth label of decision "eloquia". The blind reader understood the noun at once ("waiting for the fulfilment of a just promise of God / for a just word or decision"). With draft 8's preposition it reads "e à espera do dito da vossa justiça".

options.label: pelo que disse a vossa justiça
options.note: D16's clause carried through. It reads well, but it makes "justice" the speaker: one of the genitive's readings, chosen for the reader.

options.label: pela vossa palavra de justiça
options.note: D16's named retreat (palavra) with the genitive as a quality. Merges elóquium into verbum.

decisions.latin: Fac cum servo tuo secúndum misericórdiam tuam
decisions.why: fácere cum, to deal with. The obvious verb, "agir", is a rule-3 trap: the vós imperative "Agi" is also "I acted". 118:65 has the same build with an object (Bonitátem fecísti cum servo tuo → Usastes de bondade com), and 118:78 turned iniquitátem fácere in into "tratar com iniquidade".

options.label: Tratai o vosso servo
options.note: Draft 7, Matos Soares ("Trata o teu servo"); the light verb yields (D2). "Tratai" ≠ "tratei".

options.label: Fazei com o vosso servo
options.note: The Latin's words; in Portuguese "fazer com alguém" waits for an object that never comes.

decisions.why: scire, beside sciéntia → o saber (118:66); cognóscere / novísse → conhecer (118:75, 79 "os que conhecem os vossos testemunhos").

options.label: conheça
options.note: Draft 8, from the stylist: "saber os testemunhos" is not a current combination and suggests knowing them by heart. Matos Soares, Douay-Rheims "know"; the Greek has the verb of 118:79 here too (γνώσομαι). scire and novísse share "conhecer"; sciéntia stays "o saber" (118:66).

options.label: saiba
options.note: Draft 7: scire → saber, kept apart from conhecer. Refused by the stylist as a collocation.

decisions.why: The Latin has a vocative where the Greek has a dative (τῷ κυρίῳ, "time to act for the Lord"): "time for acting, Lord" — whether the Lord is to act or the psalmist is left open. Matos Soares closes it ("É tempo, Senhor, de procederes (com rigor)"). "Agir" is safe here as an infinitive.

options.label: É tempo de agir, Senhor
options.note: Draft 7: the copula supplied, the agent left open as in the Latin. The same words stand in the Diurnal (from the Hebrew) — it is simply what the phrase is in Portuguese.

options.label: Tempo de agir, Senhor
options.note: Verbless, as the Latin. Abrupt in a way the Latin is not.

options.label: É tempo de agirdes, Senhor
options.note: With Matos Soares and Douay-Rheims' tradition of reading the Lord as agent. Closes what the Latin leaves open.

decisions.why: dissipáre, to scatter, and so to demolish, bring to nothing (διεσκέδασαν). In Portuguese "dissipar" is said of fog, doubts and fortunes.

options.label: dissiparam
options.note: Draft 7: the Latin's word and its image of scattering (Matos Soares, Douay-Rheims "dissipated"). Unusual with "lei", as it is in Latin.

options.label: desfizeram
options.note: The plain verb for undoing; the scattering is lost.

options.label: violaram
options.note: The Diurnal (from the Hebrew). What one usually does to a law; another word's meaning.

decisions.why: dirígere → dirigir (118:5 Útinam dirigántur viæ meæ → sejam dirigidos). The form is an imperfect passive, which can also be middle (the Greek κατωρθούμην, I was kept straight).

options.label: eu me dirigia para
options.note: Draft 8. The stylist heard the passive "era dirigido a" as mechanical, and offered "me orientava para" — another verb. The middle reading of dirigébar keeps the glossary's verb and is as good Latin as the passive (the Greek κατωρθούμην is middle or passive alike). The Latinist had passed the passive; he reads this draft again.

options.label: eu era dirigido a
options.note: Draft 7: the passive, as 118:5 and Douay-Rheims ("was I directed"). The blind reader supplied God as the agent, which is a fair reading of the Latin. Mechanical to the stylist.

decisions.why: dicéntes is plural and agrees with óculi: in the Latin it is the eyes that say "When will you comfort me?". The Portuguese gerund has no number, and the blind reader attached it to the speaker ("Eu dizia").

options.label: dizendo
options.note: Kept: participle for participle (Douay-Rheims "saying"). The only grammatical subject in the verse is "os meus olhos", so the Latin's image is there for whoever looks; the looser hearing prays the same prayer.

options.label: e diziam
options.note: A finite plural verb would pin the saying on the eyes (grammar, D2). It adds "e" and turns a circumstance into a second event.

decisions.why: tota die is "all day long" (ὅλην τὴν ἡμέραν). In Brazilian speech "todo o dia" and "todo dia" (every day) are hardly told apart, and the blind reader heard draft 7 as "every day".

options.label: o dia todo
options.note: Draft 8: cannot be heard as "every day".

options.label: todo o dia
options.note: Draft 7 (Matos Soares, the Diurnal). Correct on the page, misheard aloud.

options.label: o dia inteiro
options.note: As clear; one syllable longer.

decisions.why: usquequáque → "de todo" (glossary, open: 118:8, 43; 118:51 turned it into "com toda a"). Those were negative clauses, where "de todo" is everyday Portuguese; this is the first affirmative one, and the stylist found "Fui humilhado de todo" not current "in that position". The blind reader understood it ("completely").

options.label: Fui de todo humilhado
options.note: Draft 8: the glossary's words in the position where an affirmative "de todo" is native (de todo perdido, de todo esquecido). Order only.

options.label: Fui inteiramente humilhado
options.note: The stylist's line. Plain; gives up the one rendering of usquequáque.

options.label: Fui humilhado de todo
options.note: Draft 7: the Latin's order.

decisions.why: malígni (πονηρευόμενοι, those who do evil): men, whom the psalmist sends away. The blind reader heard the cognate first as "evil spirits or demons" — in Brazilian church speech "o maligno" is the devil.

options.label: malvados
options.note: Draft 8: the plain Brazilian word for wicked people, of disposition and deed alike (Lewis & Short for malígnus: "ill-disposed, wicked, malicious"); paroxytone; heard only of persons. Cost: it is also the word of children's stories.

options.label: malignos
options.note: Draft 7: the cognate (Matos Soares; Douay-Rheims "ye malignant"), and the wording the word study had pencilled. Heard as demons.

options.label: malfeitores
options.note: The Diurnal's word, and the Greek participle's sense (evil-doers). In Brazil a "malfeitor" is a criminal.

choices.118:1: Beáti → 'Bem-aventurados' (glossary, beátus vir): six syllables for three, so both this colon and 118:2's run long (+5, +2); accepted. ámbulant → 'andam', not 'caminham', which would make an echo with 'caminho' that neither the Latin (via / ámbulant) nor the Greek has. 'os que' resumes the relative after the asterisk. The (Aleph) label is not reproduced.
choices.118:2: Two verbs of seeking in one verse, kept apart: scrutántur → 'sondam', exquírunt → 'procuram' (decisions). in toto corde → 'de todo o coração', the Portuguese idiom, set for the six places the phrase has in the psalm. The second colon has no 'qui' in the Latin and none here. The ambiguity reader asked whose 'seus testemunhos' and whom 'o procuram': the Lord of 118:1, as in the Latin (ejus … eum), and that is what was heard.
choices.118:3: Non enim qui … ambulavérunt: the negative is moved to the verb, where Portuguese wants it. enim → 'Pois' (as Ps 53:6). operári iniquitátem → 'praticar a iniquidade' (Matos Soares 1932): the phrase is frequent (qui operámini iniquitátem, 6:9 …) and this can serve it; 'obrar' was refused (archaic, and coarse in Brazil). The perfect kept: 'não andaram'. One of the six verses of the psalm with no law-word; it has via instead. 'nos seus caminhos' could be heard of the evildoers' own ways; the Latin's ejus has the same reach back to 118:1, and the reader took it rightly.
choices.118:4: mandáta … custodíri: the Latin passive infinitive becomes 'que … se guardem', which keeps 'os vossos mandamentos' right after 'mandastes' as in the Latin; 3 syllables over. An active infinitive ('guardar à risca os vossos mandamentos') would be the right length and lose the adjacency.
choices.118:5: Draft 2 takes the stylist's line (decision 'v5'). Útinam → 'Oxalá' (Matos Soares 1932). dirígere returns at 118:128 and 118:133. The colon that holds 'preceitos' runs short wherever the term occurs (justificatiónes 7 syllables, preceitos 3): 118:8, 12, 16, 20, 23; accepted psalm-wide, see words/ps118-terms.md.
choices.118:6: perspéxero is a future perfect; the Portuguese future subjunctive ('quando eu fitar') is the natural tense after 'quando'. 'eu' is named because 'fitar' alone is also third person. Draft 2: confúndi → 'ser envergonhado' (decision 'confundi'); 5 syllables over, accepted. 'fitar' was heard as paying close attention, which is perspícere.
choices.118:7: Confitébor tibi → 'Eu vos darei graças' (D5, settled; the same wording as the glossary's 117:21). in directióne cordis → 'na retidão do coração'. judícia justítiæ tuæ → 'os juízos da vossa justiça': this phrase returns at 118:106, 160, 164 and must be identical there; 118:62 (judícia justificatiónis tuæ) is a different Latin and must not be.
choices.118:8: Object-first in the Latin; natural order here (D2). derelínquere → 'abandonar' (the verb 21:2 will want). usquequáque (ἕως σφόδρα, utterly) → 'de todo'; it returns at 118:43, 51, 107. Matos Soares' 'jamais' is another sense. The ambiguity reader heard 'de todo' first as 'in no way', second as 'completely'; usquequáque bears both (Douay-Rheims 'utterly').
choices.118:9: adolescéntior is a comparative standing for the Greek νεώτερος, 'a young man': 'o jovem' (Matos Soares 1932, Douay-Rheims). córrigit is present in the Latin (the Greek has a future): followed. córrigit → 'corrige', the cognate; 'endireita' would be the image. The (Beth) label is not reproduced. Draft 2: subject before verb (decision 'v9a').
choices.118:11: peccem tibi, a dative → 'pecar contra vós' (grammar). ut non → 'para não' with the infinitive.
choices.118:12: 'Bendito sois, Senhor' — bare vocative (glossary). doce me justificatiónes tuas comes again word for word at 118:26 (and 118:64, 68, 124, 135 with the order changed): 'ensinai-me os vossos preceitos' is set as the formula; 'ensinai' is safe under rule 3.
choices.118:13: In lábiis meis → 'Com os meus lábios' (the instrument; Douay-Rheims 'With my lips', Matos Soares 'Com os meus lábios'). The Latin's comma before the asterisk is kept. pronuntiáre → 'pronunciar' (again at 118:172); enuntiáre in 118:26 is a different Latin verb for the same Greek one and gets a different word.
choices.118:14: delectátus sum → 'me deleitei'. 'como em todas as riquezas' word for word.
choices.118:15: First colon 3 over: 'mandamentos' and 'me exercitarei' are both longer than their Latin; accepted (see decisions 'mandata', 'exerceri').

choices.118:103: The plural elóquia → "os vossos ditos" (D16), as 118:11 — refused by the stylist here for the first time ("suggests maxims or loose expressions"; he wants "palavras"); kept under D16, see decision "quam" and the audit. Draft 8 takes his order. super mel ori meo → "mais que o mel à minha boca": the two datives (fáucibus meis … ori meo) are built alike. The Greek adds "and honeycomb"; the Latin does not.
choices.118:104: A mandátis tuis → "Pelos vossos mandamentos" (Douay-Rheims "By thy commandments"): from them comes the understanding. proptérea → "por isso" (118:67). odívi → "odiei". "todo caminho de iniquidade": "todo" without article = every.
choices.118:105: The copula supplied once, in the first colon. lumen → luz (glossary). sémitis meis → "as minhas veredas" (D15), plural as the Latin. pédibus → "pés" (the image; the Diurnal and Matos Soares have "passos").
choices.118:106: judícia justítiæ tuæ → "os juízos da vossa justiça", identical with 118:7 as the glossary requires. The asterisk falls after the two verbs, as in the Latin; the first colon is short (five syllables for the Latin's six). Draft 8: státui → "resolvi" (decision "statui"). The Latin's comma after Jurávi is kept.
choices.118:107: Decision "usq107" (draft 8: "Fui de todo humilhado"). secúndum verbum tuum → "segundo a vossa palavra" (formula, = the Nunc dimittis). humiliáre → humilhar.
choices.118:108: Decisions "voluntaria" and "beneplacita" (draft 8: "Fazei que vos agradem"). The blind reader heard "the prayers and praises I utter of my own accord", which is the verse. judícia tua doce me → "ensinai-me os vossos juízos" (the build of the formula doce me justificatiónes tuas).
choices.118:109: Copula supplied ("está"). in mánibus meis: the Latin's reading (first person), kept. The blind reader heard "I have control of, or responsibility for, my soul's fate" before "my life is constantly at risk", which is what the idiom means (Matos Soares explains it in a footnote). Left: the Latin gives the image and no more, and any cure would be an explanation (D2).
choices.118:110: Decisions "posuerunt" and "erravi". et → "e", though the sense is adversative: the Latin says et.
choices.118:111: Hereditáte acquisívi → "Adquiri por herança" (acquírere is simply to acquire; Douay-Rheims "purchased" is over-literal). Draft 8: "eternamente" moved inside the colon, from the stylist, who heard it as a late addition at the end. exsultátio → exultação (glossary). "Adquiri" is a first-person past that equals the vós imperative of adquirir — the reverse of rule 3's trap; no reader took it for a command.
choices.118:112: Decision "faciendas". Draft 8: "eternamente" before the object (stylist), so that the long first colon arrives on "preceitos". propter retributiónem → "por causa da retribuição" (glossary retribútio → retribuição; the Latin's reading, not the Hebrew's "to the end"): the blind reader heard "to receive a reward from God" first.
choices.118:113: Iníquos: the Latin's (and Greek's) reading, not the Hebrew's "the double-minded". Decision "odio_habui": draft 8 has the Latin word for word, "Aos iníquos tive ódio". dilígere → amar, perfect kept (118:47).
choices.118:114: Adjútor et suscéptor meus es tu → "Vós sois o meu auxílio e o meu amparo": natural order; the possessive is said with each noun, because "o meu auxílio e amparo" would fuse the two into one title. suscéptor → amparo (D19). Second colon = 118:81b.
choices.118:115: Declináte a me → "Apartai-vos de mim" (declináre a → apartar-se de, as the word study fixed). Decision "maligni": draft 8 "malvados", because "malignos" was heard as demons. scrutábor → sondarei. mandáta Dei mei: the only place in the psalm where God is spoken of in the third person to others.
choices.118:116: The formula secúndum elóquium tuum → "segundo o que dissestes" (D16): no reader remarked on it, and the stylist's own proposed line keeps it. et vivam → "e viverei" (as 118:77). Decisions "suscipe", "exspectare" (draft 8: "no que aguardo"); non confúndas me → "não me envergonheis" (D15).
choices.118:117: salvus ero → "serei salvo". semper → sempre; "sempre" moved before the law-word, as in 118:44, so that the verse closes on "preceitos".
choices.118:118: spérnere → desprezar (shares the word with contémptus → desprezo, 118:22). cogitátio → pensamento (cogitáre → pensar em, 118:59). Copula supplied. The Greek has "from your precepts" here; the Latin has judíciis, followed.
choices.118:119: Decision "praevaricantes". ídeo → "por isso", the same as proptérea (118:104, 128): the Greek has one phrase (διὰ τοῦτο) for both, and in 118:127–128 the two stand in neighbouring verses, both "Por isso" (as Matos Soares).
choices.118:120: carnes meas → "as minhas carnes", plural kept (Matos Soares). Decisions "confige", "timui120". timor … tímui: "temor … temi", the echo kept.
choices.118:122: in bonum → "para o bem". supérbi → soberbos. 118:122 is one of the six verses of the psalm with none of the eight law-words.
choices.118:123: The verse gathers 118:81 and 118:82 into one (salutáre + elóquium after defícere in), so it uses their wording. Decision "v123b".
choices.118:124: Decision "fac_cum". justificatiónes tuas doce me → "ensinai-me os vossos preceitos" — the formula, though the Latin reorders it (as ruled for 118:64).
choices.118:125: "Eu sou o vosso servo": article with the possessive (rule 5). Da mihi intelléctum → "dai-me entendimento" (formula), here with ut, not et. Draft 8: sciam → "conheça" (decision "sciam").
choices.118:126: Decisions "tempus_faciendi", "dissipaverunt". The blind reader heard "it is time for the Lord to act" first and "for me / us to act" second: the Latin's openness, kept.
choices.118:127: super aurum et topázion → "mais que o ouro e o topázio": the Latin's (and Greek's) topaz, not the Hebrew's fine gold.
choices.118:128: ad ómnia mandáta tua → "para todos os vossos mandamentos". The second colon is the near-twin of 118:104b (viam iniquitátis / viam iníquam): "todo caminho de iniquidade" / "todo caminho iníquo" keep the Latin's difference, and so now do "odiei" / "tive ódio". Decisions "dirigebar" (draft 8: the middle, "eu me dirigia para"), "odio_habui".

outcomes.remark: 'não serei confundido' heard first as 'I shall not be confused'
'não me deixeis confundido' heard first as 'do not let me be confused'
the function of 'dos vossos mandamentos' after 'rejeiteis' is unclear

outcomes.remark: 'preceitos' listed as an unknown word at each of its ten places

outcomes.remark: 'cobiçou desejar': desired to desire, or desired intensely

outcomes.reason: tǽdium is the same word; dormitáre must stay apart from dormíre.

outcomes.remark: 'confirmai-me': make me firm, or give me confirmation
outcomes.reason: The right sense was heard first.

outcomes.remark: "dito" gives the close the tone of a reference to a saying or maxim → "segundo a vossa palavra"
outcomes.reason: D15 rules "dito"; the brief forbids improvising on it. Recorded as the verdict of the test.

outcomes.remark: "vosso dito" is bookish → "a vossa palavra me vivificou"
"dito" is not spontaneous in the mouth of one who begs → "segundo a vossa palavra"
"guardar um dito" is to keep a phrase in memory → "guardei a vossa palavra"
"dito ao vosso servo" can be heard as a participle whose noun is missing → "segundo a vossa palavra ao vosso servo"
"Faça-se a vossa misericórdia" is a hard construction → "Que a vossa misericórdia seja para meu consolo"
outcomes.reason: Fiat → "Seja" is taken; the verb consolétur is kept as a verb ("para me consolar"); his full line is the second option.

outcomes.remark: "Faça-se o meu coração imaculado" is assembled on a foreign syntax → "Que o meu coração seja imaculado"
"de todo da minha boca" tangles the complements → "… a palavra da verdade por completo"
outcomes.reason: Mended by order alone ("E da minha boca não tireis de todo …"); "por completo" is refused so that usquequáque keeps its one rendering.

outcomes.remark: "agiam de todo iniquamente" is heavy → "agiam com total iniquidade"
outcomes.reason: Taken as "com toda a iniquidade", which keeps the "todo" of usquequáque.

outcomes.remark: the ellipsis "e não perturbado" is heard as a correction → "Estou preparado e não estou perturbado"
outcomes.reason: A full second verb is given, but the Latinist's ("não fui perturbado"), whose remark was major.

outcomes.remark: too much breath; "me fizeram iniquidade" is not current syntax → "Envergonhem-se os soberbos, pois injustamente me trataram com iniquidade"
outcomes.reason: Taken but for "pois" (quia is "porque" throughout).

outcomes.remark: the verse ends on a proparoxytone → "pelos séculos dos séculos e para sempre"
outcomes.reason: It inverts the Latin's climb, and the Latin ends on a proparoxytone too (sǽculi).

outcomes.remark: "dignos de canto" sounds like a literary judgement → "próprios para o canto"
outcomes.reason: cantábilis is a judgement (worthy to be sung); "próprios para" says less.

outcomes.remark: "ter parte com" asks "part in what?" → "Sou companheiro de"
outcomes.reason: The blind reader understood it at once; it is the Latin's word taken apart, and "companheiro" is another image.

audit.note: Draft 4, 118:33–80, Portuguese only. 56 items and 15 "unknown words" (9 distinct: sondarei, vereda, vivificai-me / vivificou, equidade, amplidão, iniquamente / iniquidade, apartei, desfalecimento, justificação — the same severe bar as in the first portion). Three real faults, all mended: supersperáre heard as waiting a long time (118:43, 74), "Ponde-me … o caminho" misparsed (118:33), "ciência" heard as science (118:66). "dito" was understood rightly wherever it stands and is not in the unknown list. The rest is the Latin's own openness or was heard rightly first.

outcomes.remark: "esperei muito nos vossos juízos" heard FIRST as "I waited a long time for God's decisions"
"esperei muito nas vossas palavras" heard FIRST as "I waited a long time for their fulfilment"
"Ponde-me por lei … o caminho" heard FIRST as "put me on the way of your precepts"
"a ciência" heard FIRST as scientific knowledge
"a vaidade" heard first as concern with looks, second as empty things
outcomes.reason: Ps 4:3's word and the cognate; the right sense is the word's own in church speech.

outcomes.remark: "os vossos testemunhos" heard FIRST as demonstrations of God's action / accounts of graces, in all four places (118:36, 46, 59, 79)
outcomes.reason: Settled by D15; recorded in the decision because the price is higher here than the first portion showed.

outcomes.remark: "Firmai … o vosso dito": confirm / fulfil what you said (first), or fix it in the servant; "no vosso temor" attaches to nothing in particular
outcomes.reason: The right sense was heard first; in timóre tuo hangs as loosely in the Latin.

outcomes.remark: "com uma palavra": answer with a word (first), or those who affront me with a word
outcomes.reason: Exactly the two constructions of verbum that the wording was chosen to keep.

outcomes.remark: "não era envergonhado": I felt no shame (first), or nobody shamed me
outcomes.reason: Both readings of confundébar are heard in the ruled wording.

outcomes.remark: "Isto": the word and hope named before, or what follows
outcomes.reason: The openness of Hæc.

outcomes.remark: "desde sempre": I always remembered (first), or judgments from of old
outcomes.reason: a sǽculo hangs on either word in the Latin.

outcomes.remark: "Isto me aconteceu": what was just said, or an unnamed benefit
outcomes.reason: As undetermined as Hæc facta est mihi.

outcomes.remark: "A minha porção, Senhor, eu disse: guardar a vossa lei": keeping the law is my portion (first), or the Lord is my portion
outcomes.reason: Both readings of the Latin were heard, which is what the verbless line was for.

outcomes.remark: "os juízos da vossa justificação": three readings, none settled; "justificação" unknown
outcomes.reason: A fair picture of justificatiónis in this verse; "da vossa justiça" is the option.

outcomes.remark: "tenho parte com todos": belong to the same group (first), or share an inheritance with them
outcomes.reason: Heard rightly.

outcomes.remark: "O desfalecimento me tomou": a physical faint (first), or loss of heart; word unknown
outcomes.reason: deféctio is as physical; "desânimo" is the option.

outcomes.remark: "peregrinação": a religious journey (first), a provisional dwelling, earthly life
outcomes.reason: The cognate's known price; Douay-Rheims and Matos Soares pay it too.

outcomes.remark: "guardar" obey / keep in memory (118:34, 44, 55); "juízos" sentences / criteria (118:39, 52); "salvação" (118:41); "esperei nas vossas palavras" trusted (first) / waited (118:42); "não tireis de todo" (118:43); "amplidão" (118:45); "levantei as minhas mãos para" (118:48); "me exercitava / exercitarei" practise / study (118:48, 78); "humilhação", "humilhado", "humilhastes" (118:50, 67, 71, 75); "Supliquei a vossa face" (118:58); "caminhos" (118:59); "perturbado" (118:60); "cordas" (118:61); "temem" fear / revere (118:38, 63, 74, 79); "disciplina" (118:66); "por isso guardei" (118:67); "multiplicou-se sobre mim" (118:69); "coalhou como leite" (118:70); "milhares de ouro" (118:72); "na vossa verdade" (118:75); "viverei" (118:77); "Sejam envergonhados" feel shame (first) / be shamed (118:78); "Voltem-se para mim" (118:79); "não ser envergonhado" (118:80)
outcomes.reason: The Latin is open in the same way, or the right sense was the one heard first; nothing changed.

audit.note: v5 (script: ps118/revise_v5.py; draft 4 is prayed.v4.json, flat text prayed.v4.vos.json). 118:1–32 untouched. Wording changed in eleven verses: 118:33 (Imponde-me por lei), 118:38 (Firmai o vosso dito para o vosso servo), 118:43 (E da minha boca não tireis de todo … porque pus toda a esperança nos vossos juízos), 118:51 (agiam com toda a iniquidade), 118:60 (e não fui perturbado), 118:66 (o saber), 118:70 (coalhou-se), 118:74 (pus toda a esperança nas vossas palavras), 118:76 and 118:80 (Seja …), 118:78 (Envergonhem-se os soberbos, porque injustamente me trataram com iniquidade). The law-term set is unchanged. "dito" stands against the stylist, six times over, by the brief's instruction; the verdict is in decision "eloquia".

Draft 5, PARTIAL hard check by ps118/partial.py: 80 of 176 verses, DO's ids in DO's order, no gaps; ids and marks match. Soft flags in 118:33–80, all accepted. Short, where a three-syllable term stands for a long Latin one: 118:33 −3, 39 −3, 48b −3, 52 −4, 56 −4, 67b −3, 68b −3, 70b −3, 80a −3. Long: 118:36 +3 (testemunhos), 42 +4 (the open "com uma palavra"; the resolved option is 1 shorter), 46b +3 and 80b +5 (envergonhado, as 118:6), 48a +3 and 73b +4 (mandamentos), 49 +3, 51 +3, 60 +4 (new: the Latinist's full second verb), 66b +3 (acreditei; "cri" is the option), 72 +4 (Boa é para mim, a copula supplied), 74b +4 (new: "pus toda a esperança", the price of not being misheard), 78 +4 (was +5). No rhyme inside a verse; the only neighbouring-finals flag is the first portion's 118:16/17 (palavras / palavras, the Latin's own sermónes tuos twice). No cadence flag: 118:44 ends on a proparoxytone as its Latin does.

Draft 5, 118:33–80 only, run because eleven verses changed. One remark, minor, and it is the one refused on draft 4: marks confirmed in all 48 verses. The gate is clean for 118:33–80 but for that refused minor.

outcomes.remark: minor (repeated): in sǽculum sǽculi is singular twice → "pelo século do século"
outcomes.reason: The glossary's formula for the phrase in every psalm; the number carries no sense.

audit.note: v6, by the main session under Gustavo’s delegation (DECISIONS.md D16): elóquium tuum, singular, “o vosso dito” → “o que dissestes” in 118:38, 41, 50, 58, 67, 76, after the stylist refused the noun in all six. The stylist was run again on 118:33–80 as critic/v6.stylist.part2.json to see whether the clause holds.

Read draft 6 of 118:33–80, blind. Of the six places of the singular it now passes four — the formula in 118:41 and 118:58, 118:67, and 118:76, where its own proposed line keeps “segundo o que dissestes ao vosso servo” — and objects in two, both about the order around the clause, not the clause: 118:38 (“firmai o que dissestes para” blurs who the saying is for) and 118:50 (“porque o que” stacks unstressed words). Both mended by order alone: 118:38 dative first, “Firmai para o vosso servo o que dissestes”; 118:50 verb first, “porque me vivificou o que dissestes”. Its ten other remarks fall on verses the translating agent had already weighed after the first stylist pass (118:33, 44, 46, 57, 60, 65, 70, 75, 76a, 78); they were NOT acted on in this revision and are left in the critic file for review — none concerns a law-term.

outcomes.remark: firmai o que dissestes para soa montada
outcomes.reason: by order, keeping the clause: the dative moved before the object

outcomes.remark: porque o que encavala palavras átonas
outcomes.reason: by order, keeping the clause: verb first

audit.note: Draft 7 = draft 6 (118:1–80, untouched, kept as prayed.v6.json) + the first draft of 118:81–128 (Caph–Ain), by the third Ps 118 agent. From the Latin, read with the Rahlfs Greek, Douay-Rheims and Matos Soares 1932 (pdftotext layer in consult/parallels/ps118.md); the Diurnal Monástico 1962 for diction only; DO's Portuguese not consulted as a witness (D12). Lewis & Short looked up for consummátio, fabulátio (it cites this very verse: "narration, discourse"), confígo, fauces, calúmnior (letter F fetched into consult/). D15/D16 vocabulary applied throughout by adding slots to the existing term decisions (justificationes, testimonia, mandata, judicia, eloquia, confundi, vivifica, supersperavi, exquirere, scrutantur, semita, legem_pone, intellectum, humilitate); 43 new verse-local decisions. Places where the Latin goes with the Septuagint against the Hebrew, all followed: 118:83 frost (not smoke), 118:85 tales told (not pits dug), 118:109 my hands, 118:112 "for the reward", 118:113 the iniquitous (not the double-minded), 118:119 "I reckoned as transgressors" (not dross), 118:120 "pierce … with your fear", 118:121–122 slander (not oppression), 118:126 the vocative Dómine, 118:127 topaz. Hard readings: defícere in (118:81, 82, 123); elóquium after a preposition (118:82) and with a genitive (118:123); consummavérunt / consummatiónis (118:87, 96); Voluntária … beneplácita fac (118:108); Tempus faciéndi (118:126). Rule-3 trap met: "Agi" (fac cum, 118:124) → "Tratai". The Hetzenauer print read is owed for these verses as for the rest.

Draft 7, via ps118/partial.py: hard checks pass (128 of 176 verses, ids and marks match). Two rhymes at mediant and final that the Latin does not have were removed by order alone before any reader saw the draft (118:92 meditação / humilhação; 118:102 apartei / lei). Accepted: neighbouring finals 118:111 / 118:112 (coração / retribuição — a suffix rhyme; both words are fixed by the glossary and each closes a one-phrase colon); and inside 118:111 "a exultação do meu coração" (exsultátio cordis mei — no other order is Portuguese). Length: long cola are nearly all "os vossos mandamentos" (accepted psalm-wide) or "pus toda a esperança" (118:81, 114; the decision of 118:43); 118:96b is +6 ("o vosso mandamento é amplo sobremaneira" for latum mandátum tuum nimis) against a first colon of −3 — the short option "é muito amplo" is in decision "latum96"; 118:95a +4 for the unmistakable "para me fazer perecer". Short cola (118:83b, 94b, 117b, −4/−5) are where "os vossos preceitos" stands for the seven syllables of justificatiónes tuas. 118:111 opens on "Adquiri", a first-person past that equals the vós imperative of adquirir: the reverse of rule 3's trap; left, because "acquire your testimonies by inheritance" is no sentence anyone would hear addressed to God.

Read 118:81–128 only (ps118/part3/). All 48 verses checked; marks identical. One remark, minor: 118:114 abstract nouns for the agent nouns adjútor and suscéptor — refused, kept as an option. Nothing on any law-term, on the D16 clause (118:82, 116), on "dito" (118:123), or on the places where the draft follows the Latin against the Hebrew.

outcomes.remark: "o meu auxílio e o meu amparo" replace the personal nouns adjútor and suscéptor with abstracts; fix "o meu auxiliador e o meu protetor"
outcomes.reason: The same remark was refused twice in Ps 117:6–7 (auxiliador is long and hardly said). suscéptor → amparo is settled (D19), and "protetor" is protéctor's word in the glossary. The metonymy is the one Portuguese prays with everywhere.

audit.note: Read 118:81–128 only. 19 verses faulted (20 remarks); worst line 118:92, best 118:94. 15 taken (several in part, or by another wording than his — each outcome says which), 5 kept as options. On D16: he passed the clause in both places where it stands (118:82 "pelo que dissestes", 118:116 "segundo o que dissestes" — his own proposed line for 118:116 keeps it), refused the plural "os vossos ditos" in 118:103 (the first time the plural is refused: "maxims or loose expressions") and the noun "o dito da vossa justiça" in 118:123, asking for "palavra(s)" both times. Three of his lines silently turn "eternamente" into "para sempre" (118:98, 111, 112): recorded on the glossary row in ætérnum; not taken, the two are kept apart on purpose.

outcomes.remark: "fábulas" is a proparoxytone at the mediant; alternative "narraram fábulas para mim"
outcomes.reason: Cured by the word instead of the order: "histórias" (paroxytone), which also answers the ambiguity reader.

outcomes.remark: verbless first colon sounds unfinished; alternative "A vossa verdade permanece de geração em geração"
outcomes.reason: The complaint is taken with a copula ("De geração em geração é a vossa verdade", D14's build). His verb is refused: it supplies pérmanet where the Latin has none, a third "permanece" in two verses.

outcomes.remark: "Não fosse que … é" needs a mental correction; the insertions in the second colon slow it; alternative "Se a vossa lei não fosse a minha meditação: * … na minha humilhação"
outcomes.reason: His build and his second colon are taken; the first colon is turned round ("Se a minha meditação não fosse a vossa lei") because his line rhymes meditação / humilhação at mediant and final. His exact line is option 2.

outcomes.remark: "me aguardaram para me fazer perecer" ceremonious and heavy; alternative "me esperaram para me destruir"
outcomes.reason: "para me destruir" taken. "me esperaram" refused and kept as an option in decision "exspectare": exspectáre is kept apart from speráre.

outcomes.remark: initial inversion and "sobremaneira" pile up literary solemnity; alternative "Vi o fim de toda perfeição: * o vosso mandamento é muito amplo"
the comparison comes before what is compared; alternative "Pelo vosso mandamento me fizestes mais prudente que os meus inimigos: * porque ele é meu para sempre"
outcomes.reason: Order taken in both cola. "para sempre" not taken (in ætérnum → eternamente; option in decision "in_aeternum").

outcomes.remark: the verb arrives late; alternative "Entendi mais que todos os que me ensinam"
the fronted comparison sounds artificial; alternative "Entendi mais que os anciãos"
"ditos" suggests maxims or loose expressions; the subject after "à minha garganta" delays the entry; alternative "Como as vossas palavras são doces à minha garganta"
outcomes.reason: Order taken ("Como os vossos ditos são doces à minha garganta"). "palavras" refused: D16 rules the plural "os vossos ditos", and merging elóquium into verbum is a cross-psalm ruling, not this verse's; it is the label "palavras" of decision "eloquia".

outcomes.remark: "determinei guardar" administrative, can be heard as an order given; alternative "Jurei e decidi"
outcomes.reason: Taken as "resolvi": the same sense, in a verb that is not also a vós imperative ("decidi"). The Latin's comma after Jurávi is kept.

outcomes.remark: "de todo" in an affirmative clause, in that position, is not current; alternative "Fui inteiramente humilhado"
outcomes.reason: Taken by position ("Fui de todo humilhado"), which keeps the glossary's rendering of usquequáque; his adverb is option 2.

outcomes.remark: "Fazei bem aceitas" is unspontaneous, and the vocative separates it from its long complement; alternative "Aceitai com agrado, Senhor, …"
outcomes.reason: The complaint is taken with "Fazei que vos agradem" (Matos Soares' build), which keeps fac; his line drops it and is kept as an option.

outcomes.remark: "eternamente" arrives as a late addition; alternative "Adquiri para sempre, por herança, os vossos testemunhos"
outcomes.reason: Order taken: "Adquiri por herança, eternamente, os vossos testemunhos". "para sempre" is the option of decision "in_aeternum".

outcomes.remark: the first colon piles up length until the final adverb; alternative "… a cumprir para sempre os vossos preceitos"
outcomes.reason: Order taken: "para cumprir eternamente os vossos preceitos".

outcomes.remark: "iníquos" is a proparoxytone before the mediant; alternative "Aos iníquos tive ódio"
outcomes.reason: His line is the Latin word for word (Iníquos ódio hábui).

outcomes.remark: "na minha expectativa" bureaucratic and ill-joined to "envergonheis"; alternative "não me envergonheis pelo que espero"
outcomes.reason: His clause is taken with exspectáre's verb: "no que aguardo". "espero" is refused (speráre's root) and kept as an option.

outcomes.remark: "o dito da vossa justiça" sounds like a reference to a quoted phrase; alternative "pela palavra da vossa justiça"
outcomes.reason: D16 names this verse as one where the singular must be a noun, "dito" available, and names "palavra" as the honest retreat for the whole term — a ruling for the main session, not for one verse. The blind reader understood the noun at once.

outcomes.remark: "saber os testemunhos" is not a current combination; alternative "conheça"
the passive "era dirigido a" sounds mechanical; alternative "eu me orientava para"
outcomes.reason: Taken as the middle of the same verb ("eu me dirigia para"); "orientar" is another word.

outcomes.remark: "iníquo" is a proparoxytone at the end; alternative "odiei todo caminho de iniquidade"
outcomes.reason: The cadence is cured by the Latin's own order and periphrasis ("a todo caminho iníquo tive ódio"). His line is refused: it would make 118:128b identical with 118:104b, where the Latin differs (viam iníquam / viam iniquitátis).

audit.note: Read the Portuguese of 118:81–128 alone (ps118/part3/blind/). 49 entries; most hear the verse rightly or find the Latin's own openness (118:84 the days, 118:85 the ellipsis, 118:96 finem, 118:112 retribuição, 118:126 who is to act). Wrong first hearings, and what was done: 118:82 "pelo que dissestes" as cause → the preposition changed in all three verses of defícere in; 118:85 "fábulas" as moral tales → "histórias"; 118:97 "todo o dia" as "every day" → "o dia todo"; 118:115 "malignos" as demons → "malvados"; 118:82 "dizendo" attached to the speaker, not the eyes → kept, with the finite verb as an option; 118:109 the soul in my hands heard as control rather than danger → kept (the Latin's image, unexplained). On D16: the clause was understood in 118:116; in 118:82 the mishearing was the preposition's doing, not the clause's (the reader's right reading was "waiting for the fulfilment of what you said"); "o dito da vossa justiça" (118:123) was understood at once. The law-words were heard as in the earlier portions (testemunhos as declarations given by God, four times; juízos as norms first, sentences second). Unknown words listed: odre, preceitos (six times), iníquos / iniquamente / iniquidade, vivificai-me, sobremaneira (now gone), veredas, exultação, Traspassai, topázio.

outcomes.remark: "desfaleceram pelo que dissestes" heard first as "lost their strength as a reaction to what you said"
outcomes.reason: "à espera de" (Matos Soares 1932) in 118:81, 82, 123 alike.

outcomes.remark: "desfaleceu pela vossa salvação": from waiting for it / because of salvation received — heard rightly
outcomes.reason: Heard rightly, but changed with 118:82 so that defícere in has one rendering.

outcomes.remark: "dizendo" heard as "I was saying", not the eyes
outcomes.reason: Participle for participle; the only grammatical subject is "os meus olhos"; both hearings pray the same prayer. "e diziam" is the option.

outcomes.remark: "fábulas" heard first as invented stories with a moral teaching
"mas não como a vossa lei": three readings
outcomes.reason: The Latin's own ellipsis (sed non ut lex tua); filling it, as Matos Soares does, goes beyond the Latin.

outcomes.remark: "os dias do vosso servo": of life, or of suffering still to come; "fareis juízo sobre": judge, or punish
outcomes.reason: Both pairs are open in the Latin. "fazer juízo sobre" was not heard as "form an opinion of", which was the fear.

outcomes.remark: "a vossa verdade": what you say that is true / your faithfulness
outcomes.reason: véritas → verdade (glossary, since Ps 90); the Hebrew-family "fidelidade" is what the project does not import.

outcomes.remark: "humilhação" heard first as being shamed by someone
outcomes.reason: The glossary row humílitas → humilhação records the same hearing from 118:50; the family humiliáre / humílitas is kept together.

outcomes.remark: "todo o dia" heard as "every day"
second reading: "you did more for my prudence than my enemies did"
outcomes.reason: Removed by the natural order taken from the stylist.

outcomes.remark: "determinei" can be heard as "I gave an order"
"A minha alma está sempre nas minhas mãos" heard first as having control of, or responsibility for, my soul's fate; "my life is at risk" second
outcomes.reason: The Latin gives the image and no more (Matos Soares explains it in a footnote, not in the text); any cure would be an explanation, which D2 forbids.

outcomes.remark: "malignos" heard first as evil spirits or demons
"Traspassai" listed as unknown
outcomes.reason: His paraphrase shows he understood it; "traspassar" is the word Portuguese keeps for this. "Atravessai" added as an option.

outcomes.remark: "Fiz juízo e justiça" heard as "I acted with discernment and justly" before "I judged cases"
outcomes.reason: judícium → juízo is D15's word, with this known cost; the two hearings are both in fácere judícium.

outcomes.remark: "era dirigido": an unexpressed agent (God) / my own attention turned
outcomes.reason: Both are readings of dirigébar; draft 8 has the middle, from the stylist's remark.

outcomes.remark: "sobremaneira" listed as unknown

audit.note: Draft 8 = 118:81–128 revised after the three readers; 118:1–80 untouched (ps118/verify_untouched_v6.py). Changed verses: 118:81, 82, 123 (defícere in → à espera de); 85 (histórias); 90 (copula); 92 (rebuilt); 95 (destruir); 96 (order; muito amplo); 97 (o dia todo); 98–100 (natural order); 103 (order); 106 (resolvi); 107 (de todo humilhado); 108 (Fazei que vos agradem); 111, 112 (adverb moved); 113, 128 (tive ódio, the Latin's order); 115 (malvados); 116 (no que aguardo); 125 (conheça); 128 (me dirigia para). New decisions: dicentes, tota_die, usq107, maligni. Held under D16 against the stylist: "os vossos ditos" (118:103), "o dito da vossa justiça" (118:123). Held against the Latinist (minor): "o meu auxílio e o meu amparo" (118:114). Because the wording changed materially, the Latinist gate is run again on this draft.
